## 1. Current validated baseline — the bar to beat

**5-voter `EnsembleSignal` core** (bb_reversion + rsi_reversion + ema_cross +
macd_divergence + volume_bb_reversion), flat position sizing at 3.3% of
portfolio per entry, SP500 universe:

- OOS Sharpe **1.12** | CAGR **16.3%** | MaxDD **-11.0%** vs. SPY Sharpe 0.58
  (17-fold walk-forward, gates 16/17)

Layered on top: the **leverage-realistic 3-sleeve blend** (SP500 + MidCap400
+ Nasdaq100, inverse-vol/target-vol weighted, `target_vol=0.068`,
`window=60`, `max_leverage=1.0`), validated 2026-07-13, still the live
`PaperTrader` configuration as of this run (`src/ggTrader/paper/trader.py`):

- OOS Sharpe **1.14** | MaxDD **-5.39%** vs. the SP500 core's own
  matched-window number (Sharpe 0.97 / MaxDD -11.0%)

This blend (not the single-sleeve core) is the current production
configuration. Any new lever should be measured against **both** of these
numbers and against SPY — beating SPY alone is not sufficient. **Every
diversification-sleeve candidate tried since July 13 (nine of them — see
§2/§4) has failed to beat this blend**, which is itself now meaningful
evidence: see §4's new root-cause cluster below.

## 3. What worked, structurally

These are methodology/infrastructure wins, independent of any one strategy's
verdict — more durable than the roster above:

- **The lab/WFO rewrite itself.** Moving from the pre-rewrite `research/`
  package to `src/ggTrader/lab/` (vectorbt-centric, DB-backed walk-forward)
  is what made every later verdict in §2 trustworthy — before that, momentum/
  tournament verdicts weren't run through the same rigorous gate framework.
- **NDH/DSR/gate discipline.** Requiring a strategy to clear a novelty/
  density-of-history gate and a deflated-Sharpe-ratio check before "winning"
  a fold catches noise-driven false positives (see the leveraged-rotation
  arc's regime-halt mechanism working as intended — it correctly refused to
  trust an unstable winner).
- **Flat, simple sizing beats conviction-weighting.** 3.3% flat per entry is
  the live config; conviction-weighted sizing (`conviction_bb`) was shipped
  and tested but "did not generate extra profit" — simplicity won.
- **Leverage-realism as a prerequisite for diversification claims.**
  Multi-universe equity blending only became a real GO (1.14 Sharpe) once
  capped at a realistic 1.0x leverage via inverse-vol/target-vol weighting —
  the earlier, more naively-leveraged version was weaker evidence.
- **Point-in-time universe membership matters.** `equity_universe_between`
  (span-union, survivorship-biased) vs. `universe_members_asof` (point-in-time
  correct) — using the wrong one silently inflates backtest results. Always
  use the point-in-time version for anything claiming to time entries/exits
  around index membership.
- **Always benchmark timing/rotation ideas against naive buy-and-hold of the
  same instrument, not just SPY.** This is what flipped the leveraged-trend
  arc's read from "looks promising" (low drawdown!) to NO-GO (loses to
  just holding the ETF).
- **`target_kind="weights"` vs `"signals"` changes which overlays apply.**
  The lab's realized-vol-targeting overlay (`compute_vol_scalar`) is wired
  only into `simulate_signals`, not `simulate_weights` — choosing the wrong
  `target_kind` silently drops an intended risk control. Check
  `src/ggTrader/lab/simulate.py` before assuming an overlay "just works."
- **Any standalone "beats SPY" or "low correlation" result must be
  re-verified on the deployed blend's exact eval window before being
  reported as promising.** Discovered and confirmed three independent times
  (PEAD, insider cluster-buying, Congressional trades, July 17-19): each
  showed a genuinely strong long-window standalone result that evaporated —
  and in every case *hurt* the blend — once retested on the deployed blend's
  actual 2021-01-31–2026-04-30 window. See §4 for the full pattern.
- **Free, structured bulk-data sources exist in more places than expected —
  check before assuming "paid data" and before building a scraper.** This
  session found and integrated five previously-untapped free pipelines:
  FINRA's consolidated short-interest API, FINRA's daily short-sale-volume
  CDN, SEC EDGAR's Form 4 (insider transactions) submissions API, the House
  Clerk's bulk annual PTR disclosure index/PDFs, and Google Trends via
  `pytrends`. All five turned out to have genuine multi-year historical
  depth once actually queried (not just their marketing-copy claims) — the
  FINRA short-interest API's "rolling one year" metadata claim was false;
  real coverage went back to 2020. Worth a concrete check before ruling a
  free-data idea infeasible on assumption alone.
- **...but a distinct class of data — point-in-time historical
  fundamentals/estimates/options and permno-keyed academic datasets — is
  reliably paid-only, no matter how many free sources are checked.** Four
  separate candidates (analyst-revision momentum, Anomaly-Driven Demand,
  crypto perpetual funding history beyond ~1yr, historical options-chain
  depth) all hit this same wall independently. It is now a fast, cheap
  pre-check (see §4) rather than something that needs re-verifying per
  candidate.
- **`simulate_weights` needs an all-empty-combo guard.** A fold where every
  grid combo picks zero symbols degenerates `vbt.Portfolio.from_orders` to
  zero groups and crashes (`IndexError`) rather than returning a sane flat-
  cash curve — fixed with a short-circuit in `simulate.py` (regression-tested).
  Relevant to any future event-driven/sparse-signal strategy (few qualifying
  symbols in some folds).

## 4. What failed, grouped by root cause

- **Signal-strength-as-timing doesn't survive contact with real cost/decay.**
  ML entry gate (P(up) anti-predictive), both leveraged-ETF arcs (breadth and
  trend-filter timing both lost to simpler/no-timing alternatives). The
  pattern: a signal that looks predictive in isolation doesn't automatically
  translate into a profitable entry/exit *timing* rule once real transaction
  costs, leveraged-ETF decay, or regime-halt dynamics are in play.
- **Added complexity underperforms the simpler default.** MTF reversion
  (6th voter), the 6-indicator ensemble, IC-weighted voting, Kelly sizing,
  conviction-weighted sizing — every attempt to make the ensemble "smarter"
  than flat-vote/flat-size has lost to the simpler baseline so far.
- **Equity diversification is correlation-capped without leverage realism.**
  Naive multi-universe blending (SP500+MidCap+Nasdaq at 1x-per-sleeve) lost
  to the SP500 core alone; only became a real win once combined with
  inverse-vol/target-vol weighting that actually deploys the freed-up risk
  budget (the leverage-realistic blend).
- **Momentum/tournament-style ranking is well-arbitraged in large-cap
  equities** — both the pre-rewrite and (unverified, soft) current
  implementations show negative/flat risk-adjusted performance.
- **Regime/volatility gates applied as a blunt entry filter don't help** —
  VIX-level regime throttling rejected; note this is different from a
  *sizing* overlay (the vol-target blend weighting, which did work) —
  the failure mode is specifically "binary gate on entries," not
  "vol-aware sizing" in general.
- **New diversification-sleeve candidates are hitting a wall the deployed
  blend has already found — nine consecutive attempts, three distinct
  failure signatures, none has moved the needle.** (July 13-19 batch.)
  - *Eval-window-drift* (PEAD, insider cluster-buying, Congressional
    trades): a long, earlier-starting backtest window shows a real-looking
    "beats SPY" or "low correlation" result that is concentrated in a
    period the deployed blend's actual validated window (2021-2026)
    doesn't cover. Matched-window retesting erased all three, and blending
    them in *hurt* the live configuration every time (1.14→1.06/1.12/1.04
    respectively — worse the "stronger" the original standalone result
    looked, e.g. Congressional trades had the best long-window numbers of
    the whole session and the worst blend degradation).
  - *High correlation to the existing core* (MAX-effect: 0.692 correlation,
    the highest measured this session — even a mechanically distinct
    behavioral-quintile signal ends up trading largely the same names/
    timing as the existing reversion ensemble).
  - *No signal at the fidelity available* (short-volume-ratio, short-
    interest): mechanically correct, market-neutral or long-only
    constructions with near-zero Sharpe and high regime-halt rates — not
    overfitting, not eval-window drift, just genuinely no edge in the free-
    data version of the signal.
  - The one-line takeaway for the next research pass: **another same-
    asset-class, same-market equity cross-sectional signal is increasingly
    unlikely to clear this bar — the diversification value being sought
    probably needs to come from a different asset class, geography, or time
    horizon, not another characteristic sort on the same SP500/MidCap/
    Nasdaq100 universes.** See §6 Rank 1-2 below, which now reflect this.
- **Deep historical point-in-time data (analyst estimates, permno-keyed
  academic factor panels, options-chain depth beyond ~2yrs, crypto funding
  history beyond ~1yr) is reliably paid-only.** Four independent candidates
  (analyst-revision momentum, Anomaly-Driven Demand, options IV skew, crypto
  funding-rate carry) all hit this same wall on inspection, despite looking
  different on the surface (different asset class, different vendor, different
  academic literature). This is now a fast, cheap first check for the next
  candidate proposed, before any data-pipeline engineering: does the free
  source expose a genuine point-in-time *history*, or only a current
  snapshot/short rolling window?

## 5. Known documentation gaps

- ⚠️ **Every equity Sharpe figure in this snapshot and in every report
  covering 2023 or later is understated by ~29%.** `SPY` is the only
  yfinance symbol carrying bars outside the 16:00/17:00 close convention
  (826 rows at 04:00/05:00 from 2022-12-27 on). Because `lab/cli.py:152` and
  `lab/blend.py:86` load `universe + ["SPY"]` into one frame, the union index
  gets two rows per trading day from 2023 (462-504 rows/yr vs the correct
  ~250), deflating Sharpe by ~1/√2. CAGR and MaxDD are unaffected. Rankings
  are unaffected (the benchmark deflates identically), but absolute values
  and DSR gate outcomes are. See
  `docs/research/2026-07-25-strategy-implementation-audit.md` §2.0. **Fix
  before the next backtest.**
- ⚠️ `pairs_stat_arb`'s NO-GO is **invalid for 2023 onward** — the same bug
  made its correlation-coverage guard reject every pair, so it selected
  nothing for roughly the last third of its window. Needs a re-run (audit
  §2.6).
- ⚠️ `insider_cluster_buy` keys off `transaction_date` rather than
  `filing_date`, a median 2-day lookahead. Direction of bias inflates its
  results, so its NO-GO stands — but the code should be corrected (audit
  §2.1B).
- ⚠️ The per-fold `OOS` column in every WFO table ever printed is a constant
  `0.00` — `composite_score` min-max normalizes a single-element list.
  Display-only; no verdict affected (audit §2.1A).
- ⚠️ `headline_sentiment` (A8) is downgraded to **provisional**: 3 folds
  (vs 20-54 elsewhere), a ~2× Industrials-skewed 50-name sample, and a

## 6. Internally-derived candidate ideas

These are reasoned from *what's failed and why* (§4) — not from external
research. For genuinely new ideas sourced from outside literature/practice,
see `docs/research/WEB_RESEARCH_CANDIDATES.md` (a separate, accumulating
backlog fed by running `docs/research/prompts/web-strategy-research-prompt.md`
in an external web-research tool — **as of this run, all 14 of its
candidates are resolved; it needs a fresh discovery pass before it has new
material to triage**). Both feed the same next step: pick a candidate, fill
it into `docs/research/prompts/local-implementation-prompt-TEMPLATE.md`,
queue it in `docs/next_steps.md`.

The don't-re-propose list embedded in both prompt files (§2/§4 above,
condensed) is kept in sync with this section — do not edit one without the
other.

**All four of the previous run's candidates are now resolved** (pairs/stat-
arb: NO-GO; PEAD: NO-GO; options IV skew: infeasible; crypto-carry:
infeasible) — the list below is entirely new, informed directly by §4's
"nine consecutive same-asset-class sleeves have failed" finding.

1. **Rank 1 — Cross-asset trend-following sleeve (non-equity: rates,
   gold/commodities).** A simple long-only trend/momentum overlay on liquid,
   non-leveraged ETFs (e.g. `TLT` for duration, `GLD`/`DBC` for commodities)
   as a 4th blend sleeve. Rationale: §4's core finding this session is that
   *another equity cross-sectional signal* keeps failing via correlation-cap
   or eval-window-drift — a genuinely different macro risk factor (interest-
   rate duration, commodity trend) is far more likely to actually
   diversify the blend than another characteristic sort on the same three
   equity universes. Cheap to build: free daily OHLCV only, and the
   `leveraged_trend_*` strategies already prove the trend-filter mechanism
   works in this codebase (their NO-GO was about *leveraged-ETF decay*
   specifically, not the trend logic itself — unleveraged instruments avoid
   that failure mode entirely).
2. **Rank 2 — International developed-market equity sleeve (ex-US, e.g.
   EFA/VEA-style universe).** Still equities, still free daily OHLCV, but a
   different macro/political cycle than any US index — a genuinely different
   diversification lever than the SP500/MidCap/Nasdaq trio already tried
   nine times over. Lowest-effort of any remaining idea (multi-universe
   blending infrastructure already exists via `ggt lab --blend`) — mainly a
   question of universe-membership data availability for a non-US index.
3. **Rank 3 — Re-test `xs_momentum`/`dual_momentum` on the current
   lab/WFO stack.** Flagged as a documentation gap in §5 for two runs now:
   the existing NO-GO traces to a deleted pre-rewrite codebase, never
   re-verified against the modern NDH/DSR gate framework that made every
   other verdict in §2 trustworthy. Zero new data-engineering cost — the
   strategy and data are already wired into the registry; this is a pure
   "spend one WFO run to close a known gap" candidate, not a new build.
4. **Rank 4 (lower priority, more speculative) — Bond/duration timing via
   yield-curve slope or macro carry signal.** A more deliberate version of
   Rank 1's `TLT` trend sleeve — instead of pure price trend, condition
   entries on a macro signal (e.g. curve slope, real-yield level). Ranked
   below Rank 1 specifically because it needs a mechanism design pass
   first (which macro series, what threshold) rather than being a direct
   reapplication of an already-proven trend-following implementation.
